### Importing Data and Packages 

```{r}
#| warning = FALSE
library(tidyverse)
library(sf)
library(here)
library(tmap)
library(spData)
library(viridisLite)
library(gt)
```
 ```{r}
 #| warning = FALSE
 # Load EJSreen data
 ejscreen <- sf::st_read(here::here("data", "ejscreen", "EJSCREEN_2023_BG_StatePct_with_AS_CNMI_GU_VI.gdb"))

# Filter EJScreen to Los Angeles County  
la <- ejscreen |> 
    dplyr::filter(CNTY_NAME == "Los Angeles County")

# Load HOLC Redlining data
holc <- sf::st_read(here::here('data', 'mapping-inequality', 'mapping-inequality-los-angeles.json'))

# Load bike and pedestrian crash reports 
crashes <- read.csv('data/SWITRS_LA/Crashes.csv')



 ```

# Part 1: Legacy of Redlining in Current Environmental (In)Justice 

```{r}
# Transform la crs to holc crs 
holc_trans <- st_transform(holc, crs = st_crs(la))

# Message verification for matching CRS
if(st_crs(holc_trans) == st_crs(la)){
    print("It's a match! :)")
}else{
    warning("It's not a match :(")
}
```


### Joining holc dataset to la_trans dataset
```{r}
# Combine transformed holc data to la county data
combined <- st_join(holc_trans, la)

```


### Main Map: 
```{r}
# Create map for HOLC grade and census blocks 
tm_shape(combined, bbox = holc_trans) + 
    tm_polygons(
        fill = 'grade',
        fill.scale = tm_scale(values = rev(heat.colors(5))),
        fill.legend = tm_legend(title = 'Grade')
    ) + 
tm_scalebar() + 
tm_compass() + 
tm_borders() + 
tm_title('Grade by Census Block in Los Angeles County') + 
tm_basemap()
    
```

### Creating Table 
```{r}
# Drop geometries from combined 
dropped_geom <- st_drop_geometry(combined)

# Filter by grade and create percentage column 
filtered <- dropped_geom |> 
    group_by(grade) |> 
    summarize(
        percentage = n()/nrow(dropped_geom) * 100
    )

# Create table from filtered dataset
filtered |> 
    gt() |> 
    tab_header(title = md('Percentage of Census Blocks per HOLC Grade'))
```

### Means & Visualizations 
```{r}
# Create objects for mean values 
low_income <- dropped_geom |> 
    group_by(grade) |> 
    summarize(
        mean_low_income = mean(P_LOWINCPCT, na.rm = TRUE)
    )

pm25 <- dropped_geom |> 
    group_by(grade) |> 
    summarize(
        mean_pm25 = mean(P_PM25, na.rm = TRUE)
    )

low_life_exp <- dropped_geom |> 
    group_by(grade) |> 
    summarize(
        mean_lle = mean(P_LIFEEXPPCT, na.rm = TRUE)
    )

```

### Visualizing Mean Low Income by Grade 
```{r}
# Plot for mean low income by grade 
ggplot(
    data = low_income,
    mapping = aes(
        x = grade,
        y = mean_low_income,
        fill = grade
    )
) + 
    geom_col(
        color = 'black',
        width = 0.6
    ) + 
        scale_fill_manual(
            values = c(
            'A' = 'seagreen',
            'B' = 'yellow',
            'C' = 'goldenrod',
            'D' = 'firebrick2'
            )
        ) +
        labs(
            title = 'Mean Low Income Percentile by HOLC Grade',
            x = 'HOLC Grade',
            y = 'Mean Low Income Percentile'
        )

```

### Discussion 

Based on the map of redlining in Los Angeles county, the data would suggest that there is a clear relationship between historical redlining and percentage of disadvatanged communities living in areas deemed hazardous (grade D). The visualizations produced displaying the mean variables of interest compared to the concentrations of grading would suggest that higher percentiles of disadvantaged peoples are concentrated in areas that are deemed hazardous. Areas that have the lowest percentage of disadvantaged peoples are deemed the most safest (grade A). 

# Part 2: Legacy of redlining in pedestrian and bike accidents 

### Filtering and Transforming Crashes Dataset 
```{r}
# only ped and bike accidents
filter <- crashes |>
  filter(PEDESTRIAN_ACCIDENT == "Y" | BICYCLE_ACCIDENT == "Y") |> 
  filter(POINT_X != 'NA')

sf_crash <- st_as_sf(filter, coords = c("POINT_X", "POINT_Y"), crs = 4326)

# Transform crash dots to HOLC map CRS
sf_crash <- st_transform(sf_crash, crs = st_crs(combined))
if(st_crs(sf_crash) != st_crs(combined)) stop('Please ensure CRS is matching!')

# Subset points only within HOLC regions
HOLC_regions <- sf_crash[combined, ]

join <- st_join(HOLC_regions, combined) |> 
  select(id = ID, region = grade)

# Summarise HOLC grades with most crashes
most_crashes <- join |> 
  filter(!is.na(region)) |> 
  group_by(region) |> 
  summarise(n_points = n()) |> 
  st_drop_geometry()

percent <- most_crashes |> 
  mutate(Percentage = 100*(n_points/sum(most_crashes$n_points)))
percent$region <- as.factor(percent$region)
percent$Percentage <- as.double(percent$Percentage)

percent
```

### Visualizing Bike and Pedestrian Crashes 
```{r}
# graph percentage bike and pedestrian crashes
ggplot(percent, 
aes(
    x = region, 
    y = Percentage, 
    fill = region)
    ) +
  geom_col(
    color = 'black'
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c(
            'A' = 'seagreen',
            'B' = 'yellow',
            'C' = 'goldenrod',
            'D' = 'firebrick2'
            )
    ) +
  labs(x = 'HOLC Grade',
         y = '% Bike and Pedestrian Crashes', 
         title = 'Bike and Pedestrian Crash Percentage by Grade in LA County')

```
